chain.label: ValuJet manuals omitted cold-weather nosegear strut servicing
chain.trigger: Neither document contained nosegear shock strut servicing procedures that reflected the guidance provided by Douglas.

chain.label: Nosegear shock strut underserviced/underinflated for cold weather
chain.trigger: It is likely that the nosegear shock strut did not extend far enough to actuate the ground shift mechanism because it was underserviced/underinflated for the cold/winter weather conditions.

caused_by.evidence: ValuJet's maintenance manual had not been revised or amended in accordance with the manufacturer's recommended cold weather nosegear servicing procedures.

chain.label: Insufficient strut extension left ground shift mechanism in ground mode; gear lever would not raise
chain.trigger: The captain attempted to raise the landing gear lever to the retract position, but the lever would not move beyond the uplock check position.

caused_by.evidence: when the nosegear shock strut is underserviced/underinflated, strut extension after liftoff may not be sufficient to activate the ground shift mechanism to shift the aircraft systems into the flight mode

chain.label: No auto-pressurization and takeoff warning horn; crew pulled ground control relay CBs H20/J20
chain.trigger: the takeoff warning horn sounded, and the first officer noted that the cabin was not pressurizing... when the first officer pulled the ground control relay circuit breakers (H20 and J20), the takeoff warning horn silenced, and the cabin began to pressurize

caused_by.evidence: in addition to the landing gear anti-retract mechanism malfunction, the ground shift mechanism must have malfunctioned

chain.label: FAA-approved QRH listed circuit breaker reset under 'Approach and landing' without the AOM's 'during taxi' qualifier
chain.trigger: the QRH does not include the specific instructions to reset the ground control relay circuit breakers after landing/during taxi

chain.label: Flightcrew's inadequate knowledge of DC-9 systems; never taught when to reset the ground control relay CBs
chain.trigger: Neither pilot recalled receiving any specific instruction about when to reset the ground control relay circuit breakers.

chain.label: Crew did not notify system operations/dispatch and used only the QRH, not the AOM or COM
chain.trigger: the pilots did not notify ValuJet system operations/dispatch that they were unable to raise the landing gear... the flightcrew used only the QRH, without referring to the AOM

caused_by.evidence: They stated that they believed that they had resolved the problem, and the airplane appeared to be flying safely and normally.
the pilots demonstrated that they did not have adequate knowledge or understanding of DC-9-32 systems to properly diagnose and respond to the abnormal situation

chain.label: Decision to reset ground control relay circuit breakers on short final rather than after landing
chain.trigger: The pilots decided that they could preclude such a loss of cabin pressurization after landing by resetting the ground control relay circuit breakers just before touchdown.

caused_by.evidence: had the pilots consulted the AOM for more detailed guidance, they might have recognized that they should not reset the ground control relay circuit breakers until after the airplane was on the ground
They believed that resetting the circuit breakers on short final approach would also satisfactorily accomplish the third QRH approach and landing checklist item.
their knowledge or understanding of the aircraft systems and the effects those systems have on each other was inadequate

chain.label: Ground spoilers deployed in flight at about 100 feet agl
chain.trigger: then he heard the sound of the ground spoilers deploying

caused_by.evidence: the pilots reset the ground control relay circuit breakers, thereby unintentionally shifting the airplane systems from the flight mode to the ground mode. The ground spoilers subsequently extended in flight

chain.label: Excessive sink rate on short final that the crew could not arrest
chain.trigger: the airplane's sink rate was between 39 and 47 feet per second just before runway impact, whereas over the previous 10 seconds, the descent rates were between 0 and 23 feet per second

caused_by.evidence: he attempted to arrest the excessive sink rate with back pressure on the control column and the addition of full power

chain.label: Hard impact in the runway 2R approach light area; substantial airplane damage
chain.trigger: the DC-9 struck the runway approach light area tail first, followed by main landing gear and nosegear... The nosewheel tires and rims separated after ground impact

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's subsequent increased descent rate and excessively hard ground impact in the runway approach light area

chain.label: One flight attendant and four passengers sustained minor injuries
chain.trigger: The flight attendant who occupied the rear cabin jumpseat and four passengers reported minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: During the 2 seconds before impact, vertical acceleration values increased from 0.677 Gs to the final valid recorded value of 2.854 Gs.

chain.label: Go-around and return landing on runway 31 with separated nosewheels, radios inoperative
chain.trigger: the airplane touched down on its main landing gear on the centerline of runway 31... Both pilots stated that they heard a loud grinding noise when the nosegear touched down

caused_by.evidence: the radio difficulties that the flightcrew encountered during the go-around were, directly or indirectly, the result of the airplane's impact with the ground in the approach light area short of runway 2R
